fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Vehicle Parking Area; Street Frontage; Unpaved Circulation Route
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Limited Side Access
fr.recommendations: Ensuring the single access point and extended driveway remain clear of parked vehicles and encroaching vegetation could significantly improve apparatus entry and exit during an emergency response. Maintaining visible address markers near the street frontage would support rapid navigation to the property, particularly given the length of the driveway. The unpaved circulation route connecting structures on the property could benefit from periodic attention to surface conditions to support apparatus movement and staging in the open areas near the main and detached structures. Identifying and communicating an alternate staging area along the access road may also support responder operations given the limited side access around the structures.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Dense Shrub Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Brush Adjacent to Structure; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Open Terrain; Fuel Continuity; Long Driveway; Vegetated Access Route; Wildland Interface; Scattered Trees
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing brush and dense shrub cover adjacent to the structure and within the immediate structure perimeter could meaningfully improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity near improvements. Creating and maintaining separation between shrubs, mixed vegetation, and the structure itself may reduce structure exposure and support suppression operations should fire approach the property. Where shrubs are scattered across open terrain, managing spacing between individual plants could reduce opportunities for fire to spread continuously across the parcel. The long driveway and vegetated access route represent an important consideration for firefighter access and evacuation; managing vegetation along both sides of the driveway to maintain clearance overhead and at the margins would support emergency vehicle movement and reduce fuel continuity along that corridor. Sustaining these vegetation management efforts over time, particularly within the areas closest to the structure and along the primary access route, could improve overall wildfire resilience and property preparedness at this wildland interface location.
